hook_text: "Times 3 then add 2" and "add 2 then times 3". Same rule? Try one number and find out in three seconds.
clip_script: A taxi: R2 to get in, R3 a kilometre. Say it in words. Draw it as a flow diagram: times 3, plus 2. Write it as a formula: C equals 3k plus 2. Make a table: 2, 5, 8, 11. Plot the dots, across then up — and they line up in a straight row, because every kilometre costs the same. Five pictures, one taxi. Now the trap. Someone says "add 2 then times 3". Same taxi? Try 1 kilometre: the first gives 5, the second gives 9. Different. One disagreement proves it. And if they keep agreeing? Write both as formulas, multiply out the brackets, compare. Two times x plus 2 is 2x plus 4 — same as "double then add 4". Matching formulas prove it for every number.
visual_style: Five panels slide in around a cartoon taxi: a speech bubble, a flow diagram, a formula, a table and a graph with dots lining up; then two formulas face off and one number breaks the tie.
pacing: Quick panel reveals, a pause on the lined-up dots, a snappy verdict on the trap.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and translate any rule into any picture.
